text: This sends an algebra homomorphism f:H→A to f∘S, where S is the antipode. S reverses multiplication, as in [Witherspoon, Definition 9.1.1](https://people.tamu.edu/~sjw/pub/gsm204.pdf#page=193), but A is commutative, so the composite preserves multiplication. H itself need not be commutative. The opposite-algebra construction records that reversal explicitly and works under the displayed semiring assumptions. Checks pass: [antipodeComp_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L80), [toLinearMap_antipodeComp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L87).
The composite evaluates to f(S(h)).
Its underlying linear map is exactly composition with the antipode.

The constructed homomorphism evaluates at h as f(S(h)). This is the concrete composition underlying the convolution inverse, using the antipode of [Witherspoon, Definition 9.1.1](https://people.tamu.edu/~sjw/pub/gsm204.pdf#page=193). Commutativity of the value algebra makes the composite multiplicative despite the antipode reversing products; H need not be commutative and S need not be bijective. Checks pass: [algHom_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L105), [toLinearMap_antipodeComp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L87).
The convolution inverse has this same pointwise value.
The linear-map presentation agrees with the stated composition.

Forgetting multiplicativity from antipodeComp leaves precisely the R-linear composite f∘S. Both maps have the same values; the opposite-algebra detour only justified multiplicativity into the commutative target. This agrees with the linear antipode and convolution identities in [Witherspoon, Definition 9.1.1](https://people.tamu.edu/~sjw/pub/gsm204.pdf#page=193), without assuming that S preserves multiplication in H itself. Checks pass: [antipodeComp_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L80), [algHom_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L105).
The composite has exactly the specified elementwise values.
Those values are used by the convolution inverse.

The inverse assigned to a character f:H→A is composition with the antipode, f∘S, following the convolution-inverse identity in [Witherspoon, Definition 9.1.1](https://people.tamu.edu/~sjw/pub/gsm204.pdf#page=193). WithConv specifies convolution multiplication on the same homomorphisms. This is neither an inverse function to f nor pointwise reciprocal values. The commutative value semiring ensures f∘S is again an algebra homomorphism. Checks pass: [algHom_inv_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L100), [algHom_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L105).
The installed inverse is the constructed antipode composite.
The inverse evaluates at h as f(S(h)).

This exposes the inverse chosen on convolution characters: f⁻¹ is the same algebra homomorphism as f∘S, wrapped with its convolution operations. It is the inverse predicted by the antipode identities in [Witherspoon, Definition 9.1.1](https://people.tamu.edu/~sjw/pub/gsm204.pdf#page=193). The source Hopf algebra may be noncommutative, while the value semiring is commutative; no inverse function to f is asserted. Checks pass: [antipodeComp_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L80), [algHom_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L105).
The named composite has the expected values.
Evaluation of the installed inverse agrees with those values.

Evaluating the convolution inverse at h gives f(S(h)). The inverse symbol refers to the convolution group, not to reciprocating f(h) in the value algebra. This is the character form of the antipode identity in [Witherspoon, Definition 9.1.1](https://people.tamu.edu/~sjw/pub/gsm204.pdf#page=193); the target can be a commutative semiring whose individual elements are not all units. Checks pass: [algHom_inv_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L100), [antipodeComp_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L80).
The inverse is explicitly composition with the antipode.
The underlying homomorphism evaluates to f(S(h)).

Algebra homomorphisms H→A form a group under convolution, with identity algebraMap∘ε and inverse f∘S. Applying f to the antipode identity in [Witherspoon, Definition 9.1.1](https://people.tamu.edu/~sjw/pub/gsm204.pdf#page=193) proves cancellation. H may be noncommutative; A must be commutative. The source proof uses no subtraction, so the displayed semiring generality is justified by the same identities. Checks pass: [algHom_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L105), [pointToGeneralLinear_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L183).
The installed group inverse is antipode composition.
The GL coordinate example has ordinary matrix multiplication under convolution.

An algebra map φ:A→B acts on characters by postcomposition f↦φ∘f. It preserves the counit identity and convolution because φ preserves sums, products and scalars, giving the value-algebra functoriality in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Only a bialgebra structure on H is needed; for Hopf algebras this same monoid homomorphism automatically preserves group inverses. Checks pass: [mapValue_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L151), [mapValue_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L192).
The value map is exactly postcomposition.
Successive value maps compose in the expected order.

The induced map on convolution characters sends f precisely to φ∘f, with WithConv retaining the same underlying algebra homomorphism. This is the concrete value-algebra naturality in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). It is covariant in the value algebra, and requires no injectivity or flatness of φ; the bialgebra structure already suffices. Checks pass: [mapValue_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L158), [mapValue_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L192).
An identity value map leaves every character unchanged.
Postcomposition respects composition of value maps.

Postcomposition by the identity algebra homomorphism is the identity map on the whole convolution monoid. The identity on the right is an identity homomorphism, not the counit character that serves as the monoid’s unit. This is the identity axiom for value-algebra functoriality described in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75), already valid for bialgebras. Checks pass: [mapPoints_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L112), [mapValue_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L151).
The categorical point map has the corresponding identity law.
Its underlying operation is postcomposition with the identity map.

If φ:A→B is injective, postcomposing characters with φ is injective: equality of composites gives φ(f(h))=φ(g(h)) for every h, hence f=g. This checks information preservation in the value-algebra interpretation of [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Injectivity is genuinely assumed here, unlike the general functorial map, and no surjectivity or flatness is required. Checks pass: [mapValue_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L151), [mem_mrange_mapValue_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L174).
The compared maps are exactly the composites φ∘f and φ∘g.
Under the same injectivity hypothesis, the image is characterized by valuewise range membership.

Changing values first by φ and then by ψ is the same as changing them by ψ∘φ. Both sides postcompose each character in that order, so the statement is associativity of composition, expressed as equality of convolution-monoid homomorphisms. It is the composition axiom for the functorial interpretation in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Checks pass: [mapPoints_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L118), [mapValue_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L151).
The categorical point maps have the same composition law.
Both sides act by the specified postcompositions.

A base-valued character extended first to H and then evaluated by an R-algebra point x:H→A equals its direct extension to A. This follows from x respecting the structural map R→H. It is the constant-point compatibility of [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75); here H is explicitly commutative, and only its bialgebra structure is required. Checks pass: [extendPoint_ofConv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L71), [mapValue_extendPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L89).
Direct extension evaluates by the value algebra structural map.
Extension is compatible with subsequent value-algebra maps.

If the Hopf algebra is cocommutative, its characters into a commutative semiring form an abelian convolution group. Swapping the two coproduct factors leaves Δ unchanged, so convolution products commute; the inverse remains f∘S. Cocommutativity is the tensor-symmetry condition of [Witherspoon, Definition 9.1.1](https://people.tamu.edu/~sjw/pub/gsm204.pdf#page=193), not commutativity of multiplication in H. Checks pass: [powEnd_add](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/DiagonalizableGroup/PowerEndomorphism.lean#L91), [powEnd_neg](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/DiagonalizableGroup/PowerEndomorphism.lean#L101).
The actual Gm commutative-points instance supports pointwise multiplication of power endomorphisms.
The same instance supports pointwise inverse endomorphisms.

This bundles all algebra homomorphisms H→A with their convolution group law as the group of A-valued points. WithConv changes the operations, not the maps. When H is commutative, this is the affine-group interpretation of [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75); a general noncommutative Hopf algebra still supplies the character group, without an asserted affine-scheme representation. Checks pass: [pointsFunctor_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L151), [pointToGeneralLinear_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L183).
The points functor has precisely this underlying group of characters.
The GL example realizes convolution as matrix multiplication.

A morphism φ:A→B of commutative R-algebras induces the group homomorphism f↦φ∘f on points. This is covariant in the value algebra, as in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). The group structure comes from the Hopf antipode, while preservation of multiplication uses only the bialgebra structure; no injectivity or flatness assumption on φ is introduced. Checks pass: [mapPoints_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L105), [mapPoints_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L118).
The categorical morphism acts by postcomposition.
These group morphisms respect composition.

This identifies the point map’s underlying function with postcomposition by the given value-algebra homomorphism. A point remains an algebra homomorphism from H, wrapped with convolution multiplication. It is the explicit naturality rule of [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75); the categorical notation does not change the order of composition or require that H be commutative. Checks pass: [pointsFunctor_map_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L169), [mapValue_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L151).
Evaluation of the functor map is φ(f(h)).
The underlying monoid map has the same postcomposition formula.

The identity morphism of a value algebra induces the identity group homomorphism on its points. This follows because postcomposing a character with an identity map leaves it unchanged. It verifies the identity law for the point functor in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75); the group identity character itself is a different object, supplied by the counit. Checks pass: [mapValue_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L158), [mapPoints_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L105).
The underlying convolution-monoid map has the identity law.
The categorical map acts by the same postcomposition.

For value-algebra morphisms A→B→C, the induced point map for their composite equals the corresponding composite of group homomorphisms. The categorical symbol φ≫ψ means first φ, then ψ, so both sides send f to ψ∘φ∘f. This is precisely the composition law for the points functor described in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Checks pass: [mapValue_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L192), [pointsFunctor_map_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L169).
The underlying value maps compose in that order.
The functor map evaluates by applying the coefficient-algebra morphism.

The functor sends a commutative R-algebra A to the convolution group Hom_R-alg(H,A), and each algebra map to postcomposition. Identity and composition laws are proved for these actual maps. This is the character functor underlying [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75); the affine-group interpretation additionally requires H commutative, while the construction itself accepts a noncommutative Hopf algebra. Checks pass: [mapPoints_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L112), [mapPoints_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L118), [pointsFunctor_map_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L169).
The objectwise point maps preserve identity morphisms.
They preserve composition.
The functor acts on values by φ(f(h)).

Two natural transformations between Hopf-algebra point functors are equal if their component functions agree on every point over every commutative value algebra. Group homomorphisms and natural transformations are determined by these functions. This is ordinary functorial extensionality in the framework of [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75); agreement merely on ground-ring-valued points would be a weaker hypothesis. Checks pass: [pointsFunctor_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L151), [pointsFunctor_map_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L169).
Components are the stated full groups of algebra-valued characters.
The morphism operation is the corresponding valuewise map.

At a value algebra A, the functor’s object is exactly the bundled convolution group on algebra homomorphisms H→A. Thus the formula specifies all algebra-valued points in the sense of [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75), rather than group-like elements of H. The bundle adds the group operations and their laws without changing the underlying collection of homomorphisms. Checks pass: [pointsFunctor_map_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L169), [algHom_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L105).
Morphisms act on those same characters by valuewise postcomposition.
Their group inverse is composition with the antipode.

The functor sends a value-algebra morphism to the previously defined group homomorphism mapPoints. This equation fixes the morphism component of the functor, not just its object assignment. By the postcomposition formula, it agrees with the natural value-algebra action in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75), with no alternate group structure or reversal of arrows. Checks pass: [mapPoints_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L105), [mapPoints_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L118).
The selected morphism acts by postcomposition.
The selected maps satisfy the functorial composition law.

This compares the functor map with mapPoints after identifying their displayed source and target groups. The eqToHom terms transport along equality of two presentations of the same group; they introduce no chosen group isomorphism. The resulting action is still value-algebra postcomposition, the points-functor convention in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Checks pass: [pointsFunctor_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L151), [pointsFunctor_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L156).
The transports use the explicit equality of object presentations.
The morphism component is exactly mapPoints.

Applying the functor to φ:A→B sends a character f to the character whose value at h is φ(f(h)). This is the elementwise form of value-algebra naturality in [Milne, §§3.1–3.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Every commutative value algebra and every element of H is included; there is no restriction to field points or to a generating subset. Checks pass: [mapPoints_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/PointsFunctor.lean#L105), [pointsMulEquiv_mapValue](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L247).
The underlying point map is postcomposition by φ.
For GL, the same operation agrees with entrywise application to invertible matrices.

Dist supplies only a real-valued function of two points. Despite its name, it imposes no nonnegativity, symmetry, triangle inequality, or condition on the distance from a point to itself. These laws belong to stronger structures. Thus an arbitrary real-valued function fits this interface without being a mathematical metric. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L102).

EDist supplies a function of two points with values in the nonnegative reals together with infinity. Nonnegativity follows from that value type, but symmetry, zero self-distance, separation, and the triangle inequality are not required. Infinite values are permitted, and no topology or continuity is bundled with this basic interface. Compared with [Faris §§16.1,16.11](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/EMetricSpace/Defs.lean#L53).

A pseudometric has finite real distances, zero self-distance, symmetry, and the triangle inequality, while distinct points may have distance zero. Nonnegativity follows from these laws. The bundled topology, uniform structure, and bounded sets must agree with the distance; they are not independent extra choices. Empty spaces are allowed. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L140).

A metric space adds the requirement that zero distance forces equality to the usual pseudometric laws. Consequently distinct points have strictly positive finite distance. Its topology and uniform structure are those determined by the metric, with no completeness or compactness assumption. The empty space is a permitted case. Compared with [Klazar, Lecture1 pp1–2](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Defs.lean#L70).

An extended pseudometric allows infinite distances and also permits distinct points to have distance zero. It still requires symmetry, zero self-distance, and the triangle inequality, using extended nonnegative arithmetic. The accompanying topology and uniform structure must be generated by this distance. Neither separation nor completeness is assumed. Compared with [Faris §§16.1,16.11](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/EMetricSpace/Defs.lean#L115).

An extended metric separates points by distance zero but permits the distance between distinct points to be infinite. Its symmetry and triangle inequality use extended nonnegative values, and its topology comes from the distance. Infinite separation is therefore allowed without weakening equality detection; completeness is a separate property. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/EMetricSpace/Defs.lean#L783).

A weak extended pseudometric permits a coarser ambient topology, agreeing with the distance topology within each finite-distance component. Lean orders topologies in reverse, so distanceTopology≤ambient means coarser ambient topology. The documentation’s “at least as fine” should read “at most as fine”; the actual condition is correct. Zero distance need not separate points. Compared with [Faris §§16.1,16.11](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/EMetricSpace/Defs.lean#L198).

A weak extended metric adds separation by zero distance to the weak pseudometric structure. Distinct points have positive, possibly infinite, distance. The ambient topology may be coarser than the distance topology, but agrees with it within finite-distance components. The ambient topology need not even be Hausdorff. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/EMetricSpace/Defs.lean#L797).

The open ball centered at x consists of points at distance strictly less than its real radius. A positive-radius ball contains its center; a zero or negative-radius ball is empty. This works in a pseudometric space, where different points may have zero distance, and requires no vector-space structure. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L369).

The closed ball uses distance at most the real radius, including its boundary. Negative radii give the empty set, while radius zero contains every point at zero distance from the center. In a pseudometric this can include several points. A closed ball need not be the closure of the corresponding open ball. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L420).

A sphere consists of points whose distance from the center equals the specified real radius. Negative radii give no points, and a positive-radius sphere can also be empty. At radius zero it is the center’s zero-distance class, which becomes a singleton only when the distance separates points. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L431).

An extended open ball uses the strict comparison d(y,x)<r. Radius infinity includes exactly the points at finite distance from the center, so it need not include the whole space; radius zero gives the empty set. The definition accepts a bare extended-distance function, so openness requires additional metric hypotheses. Compared with [Faris §§16.1,16.11](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/EMetricSpace/Defs.lean#L64).

An extended closed ball contains points with d(y,x)≤r. At infinite radius it is the whole space, including points infinitely far away; this differs from an extended open ball of infinite radius. The definition only needs an extended-distance function, so its name alone does not guarantee topological closedness. Compared with [Faris §§16.1,16.11](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/EMetricSpace/Defs.lean#L529).

Distances in a pseudometric space are nonnegative, even though the underlying distance function has real values and nonnegativity is not assumed separately. Symmetry and the triangle inequality give 0≤2d(x,y). Separation is unnecessary, so the conclusion allows distance zero between distinct points and does not assert strict positivity. Compared with [Klazar, Exercise1](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/MAIII_lec1_26.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L251).

Every point has distance zero from itself in a pseudometric space. This is the diagonal condition, not the stronger assertion that only equal points can be at zero distance. Distinct points may still have distance zero, and the result needs no completeness, compactness, or algebraic structure on the space. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L202).

Distance is unchanged when its two endpoints are exchanged. This symmetry is part of the pseudometric assumptions and does not require distinct points or positive distance. It would fail for a general asymmetric distance function, even if that function satisfied the triangle inequality; no such asymmetry is permitted here. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L205).

The distance from x to z is at most the distance from x to y plus the distance from y to z. This is the triangle inequality for arbitrary points of a pseudometric space. No three points need be distinct, and neither separation nor an underlying vector-space geometry is required. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L212).

A closed ball of radius zero in a metric space is exactly the singleton containing its center. Nonnegative distances reduce its membership condition to distance zero, and metric separation then forces equality. The metric assumption matters: in a pseudometric space several distinct points may belong to this zero-radius ball. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Defs.lean#L134).

The sphere of radius zero in a metric space consists exactly of its center. This follows from the equivalence between zero distance and equality, without any vector-space assumption. Separation is essential: a pseudometric’s zero-radius sphere can contain distinct points at distance zero. Positive-radius spheres are not asserted to be nonempty. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Defs.lean#L136).

An open ball is empty exactly when its real radius is nonpositive. Nonnegativity of distance rules out membership for such radii; for a positive radius, the center itself belongs. The statement already holds for pseudometrics, including spaces where distinct points have distance zero, and makes no separation or completeness assumption. Compared with [Faris §16.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L389).

For a first-quadrant chain bicomplex in any abelian category, the row filtration gives row homology and converges to total homology. Lean calls its first page “2”: at (p,q) it is H_k(row q), where p+2q+k=0. Chain degree n becomes −n; totalization alternates the vertical sign by column. Convergence means stabilization to successive filtration quotients. See [Weibel §5.6.2, pp.142–143](https://math.mit.edu/~hrm/palestine/weibel/05-spectral_sequences.pdf#page=23) and [the construction and comparisons](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/SpectralSequence/Bicomplex.lean#L406). The [roadmap S.1](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4adc7e3d0b68a8bb9974126e7411667cb533255f/TauCetiRoadmap/DerivedModuleAlgebra/README.md#L2315) Checks concern the further cohomological E₂/edge-map package, not this first-page construction; none are certified here. The existing [Čech–singular application](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/Cech/SpectralSequence.lean#L110) supplies native evidence.
